label: DISORDER
definition: A motor speech disorder in which weakness, slowness, or poor coordination of the speech muscles, caused by damage to the central or peripheral nervous system, impairs respiration, phonation, resonance, articulation, and/or prosody, while language itself is intact.

label: DISORDER
definition: Dysarthria caused by bilateral upper motor neuron damage, typically with strained-strangled voice, slow rate, hypernasality, and imprecise consonants; the dysarthria type most often associated with spastic cerebral palsy.

label: DISORDER
definition: Dysarthria caused by lower motor neuron damage (cranial or spinal nerves), characterized by weakness, breathiness, hypernasality, and nasal emission.

label: DISORDER
definition: Dysarthria caused by cerebellar damage, with irregular articulatory breakdowns, excess and equal stress, and poorly coordinated, scanning speech.

label: DISORDER
definition: Dysarthria associated with basal ganglia control-circuit damage, typically in Parkinson's disease, with reduced loudness, monopitch, short rushes of speech, and imprecise consonants.

label: DISORDER
definition: Dysarthria caused by involuntary movements from basal ganglia disorders (e.g., chorea, dystonia), producing variable rate, loudness, and articulation.

label: DISORDER
definition: Dysarthria combining features of two or more single dysarthria types, as in ALS (spastic-flaccid) or multiple sclerosis (ataxic-spastic).

label: DISORDER
definition: A group of permanent, non-progressive disorders of movement and posture caused by injury to or abnormal development of the immature brain before, during, or shortly after birth; speech is frequently affected by dysarthria.

label: DISORDER
alternate_terms: spastic CP; spastic diplegia; spastic quadriplegia; spastic hemiplegia
definition: The most common subtype of cerebral palsy, marked by increased muscle tone (spasticity); classified by the limbs involved (diplegia, hemiplegia, quadriplegia).

label: DISORDER
alternate_terms: athetoid cerebral palsy; dyskinetic CP; athetoid CP
definition: A subtype of cerebral palsy with involuntary, uncontrolled movements (athetosis, chorea, dystonia) caused mainly by basal ganglia injury.

label: DISORDER
definition: A progressive neurodegenerative disease caused by loss of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra, with tremor, rigidity, slowness of movement, and often hypokinetic dysarthria.

label: DISORDER
definition: A progressive, usually fatal degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons causing weakness, atrophy, dysphagia, and mixed spastic-flaccid dysarthria.

label: DISORDER
definition: An autoimmune disease in which demyelination of the central nervous system causes variable neurological symptoms, including ataxic and spastic dysarthria.

label: DISORDER
definition: Sudden loss of neurological function caused by interrupted blood supply (ischemia) or bleeding in the brain; a frequent cause of acquired dysarthria and aphasia in adults.

label: DISORDER
definition: Brain damage caused by an external mechanical force, such as a blow to the head; a cause of acquired dysarthria.

label: DISORDER
alternate_terms: acquired apraxia of speech; verbal apraxia
definition: A motor speech disorder in which the planning or programming of speech movements is impaired, without weakness of the speech muscles.

label: DISORDER
definition: A pediatric motor speech disorder affecting the precision and consistency of speech movements because of impaired motor planning, in the absence of neuromuscular deficits.

label: DISORDER
definition: A speech disorder caused by impaired planning, programming, control, or execution of speech movements; the two main types are dysarthria and apraxia of speech.

label: DISORDER
definition: An acquired language disorder, usually after left-hemisphere damage, impairing the comprehension and/or production of spoken or written language; distinct from dysarthria, which affects speech motor control.

label: DISORDER
definition: Difficulty swallowing, often co-occurring with dysarthria because both involve the oral and pharyngeal musculature.

label: DISORDER
definition: Impaired voice production, with abnormal pitch, loudness, or voice quality, resulting from structural, neurological, or functional causes.
flag: voice disorder as DISORDER, while breathiness etc. are SPEECH_FEATURE

label: DISORDER
definition: A chromosomal disorder caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21, associated with hypotonia, intellectual disability, and frequent speech and motor speech disorders.

label: DISORDER
definition: An inherited neurodegenerative disease causing chorea, cognitive decline, and hyperkinetic dysarthria.

label: DISORDER
definition: Velocity-dependent increase in muscle tone caused by upper motor neuron damage; the defining motor sign of spastic cerebral palsy and spastic dysarthria.
flag: a clinical motor sign; DISORDER includes motor signs by definition

label: DISORDER
definition: A movement disorder with sustained or intermittent involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal postures or twisting movements; common in dyskinetic cerebral palsy.
flag: a clinical motor sign; DISORDER includes motor signs by definition

label: DISORDER
definition: Impaired coordination of voluntary movement, usually from cerebellar damage; in speech it produces ataxic dysarthria.
flag: a clinical motor sign; DISORDER includes motor signs by definition

label: DISORDER
definition: A group of diseases in which upper and/or lower motor neurons degenerate, including ALS; often causes spastic and/or flaccid dysarthria.

label: DISORDER
definition: A subtype of cerebral palsy caused mainly by cerebellar injury, with impaired balance and coordination; speech may show ataxic features.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The degree to which a speaker's intended message is understood by a listener; the primary functional outcome measure in dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: Excessive nasal resonance on oral speech sounds because the velopharyngeal port does not close adequately; common in spastic and flaccid dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: Consonants produced with reduced accuracy or distorted place or manner of articulation; one of the most frequent perceptual features across dysarthria types.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
alternate_terms: speaking rate; rate of speech; articulation rate
definition: How fast a person speaks, usually measured in syllables or words per unit time (articulation rate excludes pauses); typically reduced in spastic dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The rhythm, stress, and intonation patterns of speech, carried by variations in pitch, loudness, and duration; often reduced or disrupted in dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: Reduced pitch variation, making speech sound flat; a characteristic of hypokinetic and spastic dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: Reduced variation in loudness across an utterance.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: A voice quality with audible air escape caused by incomplete vocal fold closure; typical of flaccid dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
alternate_terms: harsh voice; strained-strangled voice; strained voice
definition: A rough, effortful voice quality caused by excessive laryngeal tension; strained-strangled voice is a hallmark of spastic dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The characteristic sound of a speaker's voice apart from pitch and loudness, shaped by phonation and resonance (e.g., breathy, harsh, hoarse).

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The rate of vocal fold vibration, the main acoustic correlate of perceived pitch; its mean and variability are standard acoustic measures in dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: A resonance peak of the vocal tract (F1, F2, ...) that determines vowel quality; formant patterns reflect tongue and jaw movement.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The area of the polygon formed by the first two formant frequencies of the corner vowels; a smaller vowel space indicates reduced articulatory range and lower intelligibility.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: Cycle-to-cycle variation in the period of vocal fold vibration (frequency perturbation); a measure of voice instability.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: Cycle-to-cycle variation in the amplitude of vocal fold vibration (amplitude perturbation).

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The ratio of periodic (harmonic) to aperiodic (noise) energy in the voice signal; lower values indicate a breathier or hoarser voice.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
alternate_terms: diadochokinesis; alternating motion rate; sequential motion rate
definition: The speed and regularity of rapidly repeated syllables such as /pa/, /ta/, /ka/ or /pataka/; used to assess oral motor speech control.
flag: a measurement from a standard task; SPEECH_FEATURE or ASSESSMENT?

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The longest time a person can sustain a vowel on one breath; reflects respiratory and laryngeal efficiency.
flag: a measurement from a standard task; SPEECH_FEATURE or ASSESSMENT?

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The production of speech sounds by movements of the lips, tongue, jaw, and velum; one of the speech subsystems affected in dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The production of voice by vibration of the vocal folds driven by exhaled air; one of the speech subsystems affected in dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: The interval between the release of a stop consonant and the onset of vocal fold vibration; distinguishes voiced from voiceless stops and is often disrupted in dysarthria.

label: SPEECH_FEATURE
definition: How normal or typical speech sounds to listeners, independent of intelligibility; often reduced by prosodic abnormalities in dysarthria.

label: ASSESSMENT
definition: A standardized clinical test that rates reflexes, respiration, lips, palate, laryngeal function, tongue, and intelligibility to describe the severity and type of dysarthria.

label: ASSESSMENT
definition: A five-level system that classifies the self-initiated gross motor function (sitting, walking, mobility) of children and young people with cerebral palsy.

label: ASSESSMENT
definition: A five-level system that classifies how children with cerebral palsy use their hands to handle objects in daily activities.

label: ASSESSMENT
definition: A five-level system that classifies the everyday communication performance of people with cerebral palsy as senders and receivers of messages.

label: ASSESSMENT
definition: A four-level scale that classifies the speech production of children with cerebral palsy, from no apparent speech impairment to no understandable speech.

label: ASSESSMENT
preferred_term: Assessment of Intelligibility of Dysarthric Speech
alternate_terms: Computerized Assessment of Intelligibility of Dysarthric Speech
definition: A standardized test in which listeners transcribe a speaker's single words and sentences to quantify intelligibility and speaking rate in dysarthria (Yorkston & Beukelman).

label: ASSESSMENT
alternate_terms: MDS Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale
definition: A clinical rating scale for the severity of Parkinson's disease covering non-motor and motor experiences of daily living, a motor examination (including speech), and motor complications.

label: ASSESSMENT
alternate_terms: revised ALS Functional Rating Scale; ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised
definition: A 12-item questionnaire rating bulbar (including speech), fine motor, gross motor, and respiratory function in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

label: ASSESSMENT
alternate_terms: perceptual assessment; perceptual evaluation; auditory-perceptual evaluation; perceptual rating
definition: Clinical judgement of speech characteristics by trained listeners, the reference standard for describing dysarthria type and severity.
flag: ASSESSMENT is defined as a *named* instrument; perceptual evaluation is a general method

label: ASSESSMENT
definition: Standard perceptual voice rating protocols: CAPE-V rates overall severity, roughness, breathiness, strain, pitch, and loudness; GRBAS rates grade, roughness, breathiness, asthenia, and strain.

label: TREATMENT
alternate_terms: speech and language therapy; speech-language therapy; speech language therapy; speech treatment
definition: Treatment by a speech-language pathologist to improve speech, language, or communication, e.g. exercises for respiration, phonation, articulation, and prosody, and compensatory strategies.

label: TREATMENT
definition: Methods and tools (signs, picture boards, speech-generating devices) that supplement or replace natural speech for people with severe communication impairment.

label: TREATMENT
alternate_terms: voice output communication aid; communication aid
definition: An electronic AAC device that produces synthesized or recorded speech output for the user.

label: TREATMENT
definition: An intensive, standardized voice treatment that trains increased vocal loudness, developed for hypokinetic dysarthria in Parkinson's disease and also applied in cerebral palsy.

label: TREATMENT
definition: A neurotoxin injected into overactive muscles to reduce spasticity or dystonia, used in cerebral palsy and in some voice disorders.

label: TREATMENT
definition: A GABA-B receptor agonist muscle relaxant, given orally or intrathecally, used to reduce spasticity.

label: TREATMENT
definition: Surgical implantation of electrodes that deliver electrical stimulation to deep brain structures to treat movement disorders such as Parkinson's disease and dystonia.

label: TREATMENT
definition: Rehabilitation using exercise and physical methods to improve movement, strength, posture, and mobility.
flag: not a speech treatment; TREATMENT covers the underlying motor disorder

label: TREATMENT
definition: Rehabilitation that helps people perform everyday activities, including fine motor and self-care skills.
flag: not a speech treatment; TREATMENT covers the underlying motor disorder

label: TREATMENT
definition: A technique that gives a person real-time information about a physiological signal (e.g., loudness, pitch, or articulator movement) so they can learn to control it.

label: SPEECH_TECH
alternate_terms: speech recognition; speech recogniser; speech recognizer; voice recognition; dysarthric speech recognition
definition: Technology that automatically converts spoken audio into text; standard systems perform poorly on dysarthric speech, motivating adaptation research.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: The standard ASR evaluation metric: the number of word substitutions, deletions, and insertions divided by the number of words in the reference transcript.

label: SPEECH_TECH
alternate_terms: phoneme error rate; phone error rate
definition: Error rates computed like WER but over characters or phonemes instead of words; used for languages without word spacing and for sub-word evaluation.

label: SPEECH_TECH
alternate_terms: mel frequency cepstral coefficients; mel-frequency cepstral coefficient
definition: A compact spectral representation of speech computed from the cepstrum of a mel-scaled filterbank; a standard input feature for speech recognition and dysarthria classification.

label: SPEECH_TECH
alternate_terms: mel-spectrogram; log-mel spectrogram; log mel spectrogram; log-mel filterbank
definition: A time-frequency representation of audio whose frequency axis is warped to the mel scale (often log-compressed); the standard input to neural speech models.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: A self-supervised speech representation model that learns from raw audio by contrastive prediction of masked latent units, then is fine-tuned for ASR or classification.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Hidden-Unit BERT: a self-supervised speech model trained to predict masked cluster labels of the audio.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: A self-supervised speech model trained with masked speech prediction and denoising for full-stack speech processing tasks.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: OpenAI's encoder-decoder speech recognition model trained with large-scale weak supervision on multilingual web audio.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: A convolution-augmented Transformer architecture for speech recognition that models both local and global dependencies.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: A training objective and decoding method that lets neural networks map unsegmented audio to label sequences without frame-level alignment.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: A statistical sequence model with hidden states; the basis of classical ASR systems (GMM-HMM, hybrid DNN-HMM).

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Transforming speech so that it sounds like another speaker or speaking style while keeping the content; used to convert dysarthric to typical speech or to generate training data.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Technology that generates spoken audio from text; used in AAC devices and for synthesizing dysarthric training data.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Adjusting a speech recognition model to an individual speaker's voice with a small amount of their data, a key strategy for dysarthric ASR.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Data augmentation that resamples or time-stretches training audio to create faster or slower copies; tempo perturbation is used to simulate slow dysarthric speech.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Learning representations from unlabeled data by solving pretext tasks (e.g., predicting masked audio); the training paradigm of wav2vec 2.0, HuBERT, and WavLM.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Automatically aligning a known transcript to audio to obtain word or phone boundaries.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Fixed-length speaker embeddings extracted from a deep neural network, used for speaker recognition and as features for dysarthria detection.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: Low-dimensional speaker and channel representations from total variability factor analysis, used for speaker verification and adaptation.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: A phone-level score, derived from ASR posteriors, of how closely a pronunciation matches the canonical one; used to assess atypical speech.

label: SPEECH_TECH
definition: The average of listener ratings (usually on a 1-5 scale) of speech quality or naturalness, used to evaluate synthesized or converted speech.
flag: a human listener rating used to evaluate synthesis; SPEECH_TECH or ASSESSMENT?

label: SPEECH_TECH
alternate_terms: dysarthria classification; dysarthria severity classification; severity classification; dysarthria severity assessment
definition: Automatic classification of speech recordings as dysarthric vs. typical, or into severity levels, from acoustic features or learned representations.
flag: means automatic classification, but 'severity classification' can be a clinician's rating (ASSESSMENT)

label: DATASET
definition: A dysarthric speech database recorded at the University of Illinois with isolated-word audio from speakers with dysarthria, most of them with cerebral palsy, and control speakers.

label: DATASET
definition: A database of acoustic and articulatory (EMA) speech from speakers with dysarthria due to cerebral palsy or ALS and matched controls, recorded at the University of Toronto.

label: DATASET
definition: An early database of nonsense sentences read by male speakers with dysarthria, with phonetic transcriptions.

label: DATASET
definition: An Italian dysarthric speech corpus of voice commands from speakers with dysarthria and healthy controls.

label: DATASET
definition: A large, community-supported collection of speech from people with Parkinson's disease, ALS, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, and stroke, created to improve ASR accessibility.

label: DATASET
definition: A 1000-hour corpus of read English audiobook speech from typical speakers, widely used to pre-train or benchmark ASR.

label: DATASET
definition: A Colombian Spanish speech corpus of people with Parkinson's disease and matched healthy controls.

label: DATASET
definition: A Mandarin Chinese speech database of speakers with dysarthria, used for dysarthric ASR research.

label: DATASET
definition: A crowd-sourced, multilingual corpus of read speech released by Mozilla.

label: DATASET
definition: An audio-visual database of British English emotional speech from speakers with dysarthria and typical speakers.
